blocks.text: Run short of energy and things shut down; run out of everything and you're eliminated.
Upkeep is paid from the energy stockpile, and whatever can't be paid shuts down. Run out of energy, minerals and spice all at once and you are out (Terminal Blackout).
Once you are eliminated, everything you own stays where it is, but nobody controls it any more: your ships stop, and your queues and research end.
Power Plants burn minerals rather than energy, so they aren't on this list.
Every consumer pays from the energy stockpile, moment by moment.

When there isn't enough for everyone, buildings on worlds are paid first, then ships and constructs, cheapest first within each; whatever can't be paid goes offline, so the dearest ships and constructs go dark first.
Shut down, a unit pays no energy and does nothing.
Ships drift, then pick up their orders again on restart; a carrier's drones keep fighting, but its rearm timer pauses.
Constructs can't fire or build, and their shields hold but don't regenerate. A Defense Battery's gun falls silent.
Recovery: buildings on worlds, Mines included, are the last to lose power, and cheap ships such as harvesters hold on longest among ships and constructs, so keep them bringing in minerals.
Power Plants restart as soon as there are minerals to burn, energy builds back up, and everything else follows.
Pausing mining or demolishing buildings cuts the drain.
